rationale:
Evidence: iterations 0 and 2 gave identical results (score 26.0449, all 60 trials off track, progress 0.04 to 0.115, exactly one line-loss event per run, max_error about 0.061 on every track). Two very different controllers and sensor layouts produced the same numbers, so the cause is probably fixed and early (start pose, a motor-mismatch bias, or the line-loss departure), not the gains alone.

Critique handling: I accept the critique's main points and resubmit the revision with no further changes. (1) The confound is real: this round changes sensor layout, kp, ki, kd and base_speed together, so a single result cannot be attributed to one cause. I accept this as a caveat, and I will attribute by the decision rule below rather than by a clean single-variable test. (2) The sensor change is kept as the diagnostic. Sensors at y = 0.06 m, x from -0.03 to +0.03 m at 0.015 m spacing, 0.016 m footprint, antisymmetric weights [-1.5, -0.75, 0, 0.75, 1.5]. The outer sensors can see the tape when its centre is within roughly 0.03 + 0.008 + 0.0125 m of the robot centre, so the spread is adequate. (3) kd is kept at 0.1, not 0.3 as in the draft. The critique's arithmetic is right: a full edge crossing with 1.5 weights can give a large signal rate, so kd must stay small. kd = 0.1 is the damping compromise. (4) wheel_track is kept at 0.12 m, reverting the draft change, so the sensing test is not confounded by geometry. (5) base_speed is kept at 1.4. The critique is right that this is untested and that the early-failure evidence does not favour a slower design. It is a judgement: 1.4 is slower than the 1.6 to 1.9 tried earlier, which failed the same way, but a completion failure costs 500 points, so it is not pushed lower. (6) kp = 2.0 and ki = 0.1 are kept. The critique gave no telemetry-based reason to move them, and they keep the integral small. The critique's point that the off-track limit is fixed at 0.06 m is accepted: a gain or sensor change must bring max_error below 0.06 m, since geometry cannot widen the limit.

Expected result (a guess): the first line-loss event moves later or disappears, max_error falls toward or below 0.06 m, and progress rises on the oval and s-bend.

Decision rule for the next round: if line-loss timing and max_error are unchanged, the cause is the start condition or a motor-mismatch bias. The next revision should then test the line_loss rule and start alignment, not gains. If error grows with steering_oscillation, lower kp or kd. If progress is high but completion_time exceeds 3 s, raise base_speed.
